text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Thursday.

LONDON - Shares closed higher for the second day running, lifted by Wall Street's recent strength as well as continued bid speculation. Dealers believe the FTSE could test its all-time highs in the next few days, provided Wall Street maintains its current upward momentum. The FTSE 100 ended 33.1 points higher at 4,051.3.

FRANKFURT - Shares perked up in post-bourse dealings, boosted by a firmer dollar and strength on Wall Street, after a rather lacklustre performance in floor trade. The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computerised dealings in the DAX index of 30 top German shares, jumped off earlier lows in the afternoon to end at 2,824.83 points. Earlier the DAX index had ended listless bourse dealings down 13 points at 2,807.75 points.

PARIS - Stocks finished sharply higher, buoyed by gains in the dollar and bond markets and takeover speculation on the bourse. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.81 points, or 1.34 percent, at 2,248.70.

ZURICH - Shares closed near the day's high after a friendly Wall Street opening. Gains were made despite pressure stemming from a fall in Ciba and Sandoz. Ciba and Sandoz, which on Wednesday won final approval to merge into Novartis, slumped more than one percent each on profit-taking and switches from shares into convertible bonds. The all share SPI closed up 4.14 points to 2,475.76 points.

TOKYO - The stock market's key index closed at a low for the year, as selling in cash stocks and futures escalated shortly before the close. The benchmark Nikkei 225 tumbled 522.36 points, the third largest one-day drop this year, to settle at 19,570.67.

HONG KONG - Selective strength in some major blue chips drove stocks to a higher close, but brokers said the overall tone during the session had been fairly subdued ahead of the holiday period. The Hang Seng index closed on a gain of 80.54 points at 12,846.56.

SYDNEY - Shares ended a quiet session near their highs following a stronger Dow from the open while firmer base metals prices underpinned the resource sector. The All Ordinaries index closed eight points higher at 2,331.7, close to its intra-session high of 2,332.8.

JOHANNESBURG - Stocks posted their second successive rise -- after a huge sell-off earlier in the week -- when they received a much needed shot in the arm from better-than-expected inflation data. The all-share index ended up 53.1 points to 6,468.0 as industrials put on 89.6 points to close at 7,724.7. The golds index held onto modest early gains to finish relatively flat at 1,491.3, up 2.6 points.
